βL*=0\beta_L^* = 0: under α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L), α≤1\alpha \leq 1 exactly when βL≤0\beta_L \leq 0; βL<0\beta_L < 0 lies outside Axiom 2’s range, whose lower edge, βL=0\beta_L = 0, gives linear growth (α=1\alpha = 1). Every βL<1\beta_L < 1 gives a power law; the exponential row reads βL≳0.9\beta_L \gtrsim 0.9 as a power law too steep (α≳10\alpha \gtrsim 10) to tell from an exponential over a finite range, and a strict exponential needs βL=1\beta_L = 1.

The boundary values are approximate, set by the original hypotheses that βL≈0.5\beta_L \approx 0.5 in AI yields a power law and βL≳0.95\beta_L \gtrsim 0.95 in quantum systems an exponential; neither value has been measured. Precise boundaries require empirical determination.

Cross-domain βL\beta_L prediction.

The coupling βL\beta_L can be independently measured in each domain. On the framework, βL\beta_L fixes the asymptotic power-law exponent; βL\beta_L near one gives a power law too steep to tell from an exponential over a finite range; an exponential needs additive composition (Theorem 1, case 2), and saturation a cap (case 3). It is a hypothesis under test, registered in part as P5 (the exponent the measured coupling implies) and P18 (the family the composition operator predicts). If a measured coupling fails to predict the observed exponent, the theoretical connection between ⊕\oplus and functional form requires revision.

Structural implication: the completeness of classical scaling.

Since, under Theorem 1’s hypotheses (associativity, continuity and the stated scalar-composition scoping), a recursive process combines its steps through one of the three composition operators, and since the Hyers-Ulam theorem guarantees stability under perturbation, the space of classical scaling behaviours under those hypotheses is low-dimensional: a choice of form (power law, exponential, saturation, or the linear and logarithmic Cauchy solutions), a coefficient, and an exponent or rate. This completeness statement follows from Theorem 1 and the Hyers-Ulam theorem under their hypotheses; it is not a separate theorem. On this reading, the phase diagram above, originally motivated by AI systems, is a cross-section of a wider diagram for the classical recursive systems that satisfy those hypotheses; the companion paper, Eastwood (2026c), develops the cross-domain connection, and the cosmological reading stands, as conjecture, at the close (Section 10).

5.5 Composition operator transitions

The framework as presented assigns a single composition operator ⊕\oplus to each system. This may be an idealisation. In bounded or dissipative systems, the composition operator itself can transition between regimes as recursive depth increases.

Conjecture 5 (Composition operator transitions). A single physical system can transition between different composition operator regimes as a function of recursive depth or an internal state parameter. This extends the framework from fixed ⊕\oplus to depth-dependent ⊕(R)\oplus(R), modelled by generalising Axiom 2 to dg/dr=a(g,r)⋅gβL(g,r)dg/dr = a(g, r) \cdot g^{\beta_L(g, r)} where the coupling itself depends on accumulated amplification.

Computational checks. Computational tests show that logistic growth, gradient descent with momentum, and Kuramoto oscillator synchronisation all exhibit analogous transitions when measuring local βL\beta_L in sliding windows. By contrast, unbounded pure-Bernoulli systems maintain constant βL\beta_L to machine precision (σ<10−6\sigma < 10^{-6}).

Implications for contradictory AI evidence. If reasoning systems begin in an additive regime (shallow thinking), transition to multiplicative (deep reasoning with cumulative advantage), and eventually saturate, then studies measuring at different recursive depths would observe different scaling in the same system. The finding of Zeng et al. (2025) that correct solutions are often shorter than incorrect ones may mark the transition between multiplicative and bounded composition. This is testable: measure local βL\beta_L at different reasoning depths within a single system. Against the registered P1 the reading is no exit: the theory registration says that the reading that a system changed its own composition operator “is not available after the result is seen”, and that the papers’ statement that a self-modifying system escapes the attention bound “is not a licence to move this proposition’s boundary afterwards”.

Epistemic status.

Conjecture 5, supported in three computational systems and untested in physical experiments, is not derivable from the original three axioms. It extends the framework’s scope but requires independent experimental confirmation.

6 Predictions

6.1 The cross-domain forward prediction

The strongest test of this framework is not whether it describes systems already studied. It is whether it predicts the scaling behaviour of systems not yet examined.

Forward prediction.

Identify a recursive system not studied in this paper: evolutionary algorithms, market price discovery, immune response maturation, protein folding optimisation, or any system satisfying the three axioms. Measure only its composition operator ⊕\oplus (by observing how marginal gains relate to accumulated capability). Measured over the early depths only, ⊕\oplus is to predict whether the system follows power-law, exponential or saturating scaling at the later depths, before the full UU vs RR curve is measured.

This is a genuine forward prediction. No domain-specific theory of evolution, economics, or immunology is known to this programme to make it (same search basis and limits as above). If the prediction succeeds in a new domain, it supports the framework’s generality there. If it fails, the framework’s cross-domain applicability is refuted. It is a hypothesis under test, and its registered form is P18, that the family that best fits a domain is the family the composition operator predicts before the curve is seen; the registration holds P18 with low confidence and marks it NOT EVALUABLE until the classification rule this proposition requires is shown to transmit to a third party.

Paper VII · The ARC Theory · Law I, the ARC Principle · Cauchy Unification: the Classification Behind the Law’s Form gives a structured prediction comparison under a publicly stated rule rather than a per-domain advance timestamp, testing this forward prediction within this programme. The composition operator was classified from known physics, then the scaling family was predicted and compared against the families that AICc model selection chose across 25 empirical domains (50-domain tiered suite) spanning physics, biology, computational systems, and social science. Under the classification rule of March 2026, on a candidate set with no logarithmic and no pure linear family and under strict AICc model selection, 19 of 25 empirical domains preferred the Cauchy-predicted family; the primary statistic is a permutation test, p=7×10−5p = 7 \times 10^{-5}, and the binomial p=1.56×10−5p = 1.56 \times 10^{-5} is a sensitivity check. The classification rule reached the public repository at 23:33 UTC on 16 March 2026, and the fifty per-domain assignments were committed together with their results at 23:54 that night, so predicting each family before its fit is true of the procedure and not of the timestamp; the domains were chosen and classified by the author. It is not a formally pre-registered trial. Paper VII’s staged tests, the fourth-cell test (Unit 55, preregistered by timestamp, first anchored on 12 August 2026) and the eighty-domain catalogue test (Unit 57), are drafted and awaiting human submission.

A twelve-domain extension of Paper VII’s comparison followed the same night, and its predictions were public before it ran: the twelve-row manifest fixing an operator class, a predicted family and a predicted model for each row was committed to the public repository at 00:19:19 UTC on 17 March 2026 in commit 8edaec0, attestation class public repository commit date, and the fits ran twenty-three minutes later, returning 10 of 12 (p=5.44×10−4p = 5.44 \times 10^{-4}). It is preregistered in substance and it is not an accepted registry submission: the twelve classifications are the author’s own, the candidate set is the pre-correction one with no logarithmic family, the packet’s own written condition, deposit to a registry before data extraction, was not met, and the author’s demotion of 00:56 stands in that half. One row repeats a domain, operator class and predicted model already public at 23:54:53 UTC on 16 March 2026, attestation class public repository commit date, with a matching outcome, so the strictly fresh count reads 9 of 11 (p=1.37×10−3p = 1.37 \times 10^{-3}), and with a second, doubtful row removed as well it reads 8 of 10 (p=3.40×10−3p = 3.40 \times 10^{-3}). Every pp here is computed under a taxonomy and a statistic since superseded, and the twelve domains are used up for any later test. It is a dated result and it is not confirmation of the laws. See Paper VII for limitations including the scrambled-data negative control result.

6.2 The within-system regime transition

Regime transition prediction.

The same physical system should transition between scaling regimes as the coupling strength βL\beta_L is experimentally varied. In AI: vary the fraction of context available to each reasoning step (e.g., by truncating the attention window). As the effective βL\beta_L varies, the fitted exponent should follow the finite-window exponent that the complete solution of Axiom 2 predicts from the measured coupling, within the margin of 0.10 that P5 registers for that comparison. This tests the βL\beta_L-to-α\alpha relationship within a single system, eliminating cross-domain confounds.

6.3 The R*R^* crossover

When plotting capability against recursive depth, there should exist a distinct crossover at depth R*=α/aR^* = \alpha/a (Theorem 3). Below R*R^*, scaling appears approximately linear. Above R*R^*, scaling follows the domain-appropriate super-linear form. Since R*R^* depends only on the architecture (α\alpha and aa), it should be consistent across different input qualities for the same system.

If separately measured α\alpha and aa place the crossover R*R^* inside the measured window and no transition from approximately linear to compounding gains appears there, the framework’s transitional regime prediction is falsified; a pure power from the first pass is the case a=αa = \alpha of Theorem 4 and refutes nothing. R*R^* is a unique signature that distinguishes recursive amplification from simple redundancy.

6.4 The ARC Bound

The bound as registered. The ARC Bound, at most two, is the inequality the ceiling relation returns from the same-class limit on the correction exponent, and it needs P6 and P20 and nothing else. That the ceiling sits at exactly two is a separate and weaker claim, which would also need P17 (the correctors on a panel failing independently), the conditions registered in the alternative baselines and a mapping the programme has not registered; the registration claims the inequality and conjectures the equality, and neither has yet been tested. Same-class means a system corrected by mechanisms of its own class (P6, which the registration holds with low confidence): a cross-class system measured above two does not refute the bound, and the corrector’s class is declared and evidenced before the run. Under the registration the bound takes its word from P6 and P20 alone. It is refuted only where P6 is refuted, by “a same-class corrector whose measured correction exponent interval lies entirely above one half”, a measurement made on correctors that needs no system with α>1\alpha > 1; it loses its derivation where P20 is refuted; and it is never printed supported, since P6 admits no supported verdict. Law III’s own test of a sustainable maximum is P3’s, against the value the ceiling relation returns from the correction exponent measured on the same system, not against two.

This paper’s own form, a falsifiable conjecture of the early framework (note: Paper X supersedes this fixed-exponent framing as the operative safety criterion by its co-scaling condition βC>k\beta_C > k; the equation U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha} and the ARC Bound are not retracted, only re-scoped to genuinely self-improving systems): a sequential system that corrects itself with mechanisms of its own class and composes multiplicatively does not sustain α>2\alpha > 2. Its test is criterion F5 (Table 9), this paper’s own, which decides nothing registered. The wider reach of earlier versions, to every classical sequential system, biological networks and economic processes among them, is withdrawn: the registration places biological and economic systems out of scope, as systems “for which the framework offers an analogy and no measurement”.

An information-theoretic heuristic (attention-based architectures). Transformer self-attention computes pairwise interactions across all NN tokens in a context window. This creates at most O(N2)O(N^2) information pathways per forward pass. Each recursive reasoning step (a chain-of-thought step) processes the accumulated context through this quadratic bottleneck. Since the information density available to each step is bounded by O(N2)O(N^2), the capability gain per step cannot exceed quadratic scaling in context length. Mapping context utilisation to the coupling parameter βL\beta_L: full quadratic utilisation corresponds to βL=0.5\beta_L = 0.5, yielding α=1/(1−0.5)=2\alpha = 1/(1-0.5) = 2. On this heuristic, Umax=I×R2U_{\max} = I \times R^2 would be an upper bound for attention-based architectures; the scope below, and corrections 2 and 4, say why it is a conjecture and not a result.

Scope: For transformer-based architectures with standard self-attention this derivation amounts to a heuristic: it tallies pathways without establishing any bound on capability, and the step it takes from quadratic pathway density to βL=1/2\beta_L = 1/2 remains conjectural. Earlier versions conjectured that it holds for classical sequential systems generally, on the grounds that any finite-bandwidth sequential processor faces analogous pairwise information constraints; that reach is now this paper’s own early-framework conjecture, tested by criterion F11, which decides nothing registered. Architectures that transcend pairwise attention (e.g., higher-order tensor attention, quantum-coherent processing) could in principle exceed the quadratic bound. On this heuristic the bound would be an architecture-relative capacity ceiling of the kind information theory supplies, not a universal physical law; the value two itself rests on the pacing derivation of Law III, the ARC Ceiling, a law under test (below).

αcrit=11−γ\begin{equation*} \alpha_{\text{crit}} = \frac{1}{1-\gamma} \end{equation*}(7)

The law.

The stability ceiling on the capability exponent is the reciprocal of the corrector’s shortfall, 1−γ1 - \gamma, where γ\gamma is the correction-leverage exponent. Corrected 16 August 2026 from the earlier 1/γ1/\gamma form, which agrees with this one only at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2. The registration states the relation as “a conditional specialisation of the second law, not a third finding standing beside it”: it is what the correction-and-burden balance returns “once the burden model fixes the drift exponent and the direct depth term is zero”, and a result on it is “never independent corroboration of the second law”. Its form is registered as P20, which has no verdict; with a direct depth term η\eta, the pacing case returns 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta) at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, and two only where η=0\eta = 0 (Laws IV and V: the mathematics, version 1.2). The relation is derived inside a pacing model and has not been derived from a joint model of capability growth, correction accumulation, error covariance, correction delay and absolute harm, so Law III is stated here as a minimal-model result rather than as a general law. At γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2 the ceiling equals two, the ARC Bound’s point value, and that value rests on two assumptions the registration names and does not present as established: the burden model, under which the drift exponent follows the rate of capability gain, and the route to one half, four conditions on a corrector’s channels (correction capacity read as inverse residual uncertainty, channels uncorrelated, their number growing in proportion to the capability corrected, and comparable in variance and quality). The independence condition is the subject of a drafted study, AH, preregistered by timestamp, first anchored on 12 August 2026 (a second, AE, has since been withdrawn from the programme); Unit 82, registered on OSF on 27 October 2026 (Section 8), tests P17, which bears on one of the conditions behind one half and establishes neither the value nor the bound. The capability exponent measured on today’s frozen models is one model’s fit and inconclusive (Paper II; Section 4.3 prints its row whole); the ceiling is not a measurement.

Law before value. The programme carries a law and a value, and they are not the same claim. The law: αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma), a self-improving system stays correctable only while correction keeps pace, and the ceiling is the reciprocal of the corrector’s shortfall. The value: γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, therefore a ceiling of two, a point value that rests on the two assumptions above and that the registration conjectures; what it claims is the inequality, a ceiling of at most two for same-class correctors. One consequence of the corrected form should be stated where a reader meets it, because it cuts both ways: since 1/(1−γ)≤21/(1-\gamma) \le 2 is exactly equivalent to γ≤1/2\gamma \le 1/2, the ARC Bound and P6’s same-class cap are one commitment written in two notations, not two independent claims. The gain is parsimony, since the theory assumes less than it appeared to. The discipline is that neither may ever be offered as evidence for the other, here or on any companion surface, because a measurement near one half does not corroborate a ceiling of two; it restates it. The law owns the ground and the value stands on it, never the reverse: if two dies, the law survives completely (measure γ\gamma, report the ceiling it implies); if the law dies, two has no independent support, because the derivation runs through 1/(1−γ)1/(1-\gamma). Two is what the law returns at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, and the conditions behind one half are what the drafted and registered units above examine.

The identity is a test preregistered by timestamp, never an established fact. The stability ceiling and the conversion exponent meet at the same number, and the temptation is to say one constant does two jobs. The claim’s status is stricter: the identity is preregistered by timestamp for testing, in advance of the data, with outcomes that can kill it. Study AE was drafted to test the reciprocity requirement between the separately measured leverage cap and stability boundary, with three outcomes per cell (supported, refuted, insufficient precision) and an aggregation rule under which one refuted cell refutes the identity, and it has since been withdrawn from the programme; study AG estimates the coupling and the correction exponent on one and the same system and tests whether the growth exponent the leverage fraction sustains respects the ceiling the correction exponent sets (βL≤γ\beta_L \leq \gamma), and is designed to find a violation. If the channels disagree, the unification is withdrawn from every surface it has reached, with the same prominence as the framing. Agreement between an asserted one half and Paper II’s regression exponent, one model’s fit and inconclusive (Section 4.3 prints its row whole), is never presented as evidence, because the two may share an accumulation law, and agreement between sharers is not corroboration.

The objection to pre-empt, because a physicist reaches it in one step. Fault-tolerant quantum error correction suppresses logical error exponentially in code distance below threshold, which looks like a counterexample to any square-root cap. Two scope facts answer it: the exponential suppression runs on the redundancy axis at fixed capability, not on the coupling of corrective strength to the capability of the corrected system, which is the exponent this programme measures; and the threshold theorem itself requires sufficiently uncorrelated physical noise, which is the independence premise again, wearing hardware. Likewise, concentration bounds give exponentially falling error probability while estimator width falls as the square root: different quantities, and conflating them manufactures a refutation.

Withdrawn derivation: Previous versions of this paper derived βL≤0.5\beta_L \leq 0.5 from a stability/elasticity analysis (the relative sensitivity βL/(1−βL)\beta_L/(1-\beta_L) reaching unity at βL=0.5\beta_L = 0.5, interpreted as an ‘edge-of-chaos boundary’ confirmed by Lyapunov analysis). This derivation has been withdrawn. The elasticity formula βL/(1−βL)\beta_L/(1-\beta_L) is mathematically correct but its interpretation as a stability boundary was a category error: elasticity >1> 1 indicates sensitivity, not dynamical instability, and an autonomous flow on the line is monotone, so it cannot so much as oscillate, still less turn chaotic (in two dimensions the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem shuts chaos out as well). The O(N2)O(N^2) self-attention count survives as a heuristic for why frozen transformers fall below the ceiling; the ceiling itself is derived from the pacing argument of Law III (correction 9).

Biological comparison. Kleiber’s Law (M0.75M^{0.75}) (Kleiber 1932) gives a metabolic-scaling exponent of three quarters; the mammalian exponent is debated (the note on d=3d = 3 below), and the derivations of αmet=d/(d+1)\alpha_{\text{met}} = d/(d+1) are set out with the dimensional ladder. Earlier versions read the reciprocal, 1/0.75=1.331/0.75 = 1.33, as a capability exponent in this framework’s sense and placed biological systems below the conjectured ceiling of two; the notation register carries no such reciprocal reading, and the registration places biological systems out of the bound’s scope, so this edition states its biology predictions in the metabolic sense only. Leaf venation (quasi-two-dimensional networks, reduced thermodynamic drag) should show a metabolic-scaling exponent of 2/32/3: a forecast this paper makes without a registered test (criterion F12).

The Dimensional Ladder. Here is where abstract mathematics meets living organisms. The formula αmet=d/(d+1)\alpha_{\text{met}} = d/(d+1), relating the metabolic scaling exponent to body-plan dimensionality dd, has been derived independently through distinct theoretical routes: West, Brown and Enquist (1997, 2004) from fractal network optimisation; Banavar, Maritan and Rinaldo (1999) from sequential flow networks; Demetrius (2008) from quantum statistical mechanics; Demetrius and Tuszynski (2010) from quantum oscillator coupling; Zhao (2022) from universal growth scaling arguments; and Bettencourt (2013) from urban scaling theory. The companion paper (Eastwood 2026c) identifies why these independent derivations converge: α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) is a necessary consequence of three conditions acting together: Cauchy-constrained multiplicative composition, dd-dimensional space-filling geometry, and a conservation or optimisation constraint on resource flow. Neither Cauchy alone, nor space-filling alone, is sufficient; all three are needed. The formula is not original to this framework. Space-filling and the conservation or optimisation constraint are premises of the derivations cited; what this framework adds is the first condition, that Cauchy’s equation confines continuous multiplicative composition to the power-law family. Its registered form is P9, that where an effective dimension can be assigned to a domain, the growth exponent follows the dimensional relation; the registration holds P9 with low confidence and marks it NOT EVALUABLE until the rule that assigns an effective dimension to a domain exists as a written procedure. Applied to biology, it yields distinct quantitative predictions, each testable against published data:

Table 6. The dimensional ladder, applied to biology.
Body plan Dimension dd Predicted α\alpha Measured α\alpha Status
1D (filamentous fungi) 1 0.500 0.5470.547 Consistent (p=0.107p = 0.107)
2D (no organism with genuinely two-dimensional transport identified; leaf venation, quasi-two-dimensional, is criterion F12’s test) 2 0.667 no data Unconfirmed in biology (not yet measured); matched in physics by one analytic identity and one unsourced reference value, and by the Friedmann matter era as an identity (see the note on d=2d = 2 below)
3D (mammals, birds, fish) 3 0.750 0.6870.687 to 0.7500.750 Debated (see note below)

The 1D value is the mean of three colony-level scaling factors that Aguilar-Trigueros et al. (2017) report at 20 degrees Celsius, 0.58 and 0.53 against biomass (ectomycorrhizal and marine fungi) and 0.53 against radial extension rate (saprotrophic fungi), comparisons its authors present as hypothesis generators on small data sets. It is labelled ‘consistent’ rather than ‘confirmed’ because the factors were measured at the colony level; definitive confirmation requires individual-hypha respirometry. One-sample tt tests of the three reject d=2d = 2 (p=0.019p = 0.019) and d=3d = 3 (p=0.007p = 0.007) and do not reject d=1d = 1 (p=0.107p = 0.107).

d=2d = 2 correction: Previous versions cited jellyfish and cnidarians as confirming the d=2d = 2 prediction. No valid two-dimensional biological test organism has been identified; jellyfish and cnidarians do not possess genuinely two-dimensional resource transport networks. In physics the d=2d = 2 value is matched by an analytic identity (two-dimensional percolation, through the absolute value of its specific-heat exponent) and by a reference value without a named source (two-dimensional brittle fragmentation, Table 7); the earthquake B-value, being a definitional identity, is no longer counted; and it is matched by Friedmann cosmological scaling as an identity, not evidence: the change of variables d=2/(1+3w)d = 2/(1+3w) maps the flat Friedmann exponent 2/(3(1+w))2/(3(1+w)) onto d/(d+1)d/(d+1) for every constant equation of state w>−1w > -1 other than w=−1/3w = -1/3, and w=0w = 0, the matter era, gives d=2d = 2. The biological d=2d = 2 test stays open: leaf venation, a quasi-two-dimensional transport network, is the test criterion F12 names, not yet run.

d=3d = 3 debate: The empirical value of the mammalian metabolic scaling exponent is debated, with estimates ranging from approximately 0.67 to 0.75 depending on taxon, mass range, temperature correction, and statistical method. White and Seymour (2003) found support for 2/3 over 3/4 after controlling for temperature and phylogeny. Kolokotrones et al. (2010) showed the log-log relationship exhibits convex curvature, meaning no single exponent fits perfectly across the full mass range. The d/(d+1)d/(d+1) prediction of 0.750 for d=3d = 3 matches the upper end of this range. The variation itself is consistent with the framework: organisms with effective transport dimensions between 2 and 3 would produce exponents between 2/3 and 3/4. The framework accommodates this variation rather than requiring a single universal exponent.

The conservation or optimisation constraint takes a different form in each derivation (energy minimisation in West, supply-demand balance in Banavar, steady-state energy balance in Demetrius); together with multiplicative composition and space-filling it suffices for d/(d+1)d/(d+1).

Paper VII extends this comparison from the instances catalogued here to 25 empirical domains (Section 6.1).

Physics instances. The formula α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) is not restricted to biology. It appears wherever a dd-dimensional hierarchical network, subject to a conservation or optimisation constraint on resource flow, partitions a (d+1)(d+1)-dimensional space. The formula matches known or reference exponents in several physics domains:

Table 7. Instances in physics.
System Dimension dd Predicted α\alpha Reference value Error
KPZ surface roughness (1D) 1 0.500 0.500 0.0%
2D percolation (specific heat) 2 0.667 0.667 0.0%
Brittle fragmentation (2D) 2 0.667 0.67 0.5%
Brittle fragmentation (3D) 3 0.750 0.750 0.0%

No reference value here is a measurement made for this paper. The one-dimensional KPZ roughness exponent, 1/21/2, is exact (Kardar et al. 1986). In the percolation row the match is to the absolute value of the specific-heat exponent that the hyperscaling relation gives, |α|=2/3|\alpha| = 2/3, a step Eastwood (2026c) flags for a provenance audit. The two fragmentation values carry no named source, as that paper records, and await the row-by-row provenance audit it requires.

These four instances carry no aggregate error figure. The sub-0.2 per cent mean quoted earlier was withdrawn on 14 August 2026 (correction 10), since averaging over analytic identities is no measure of predictive accuracy, and the earthquake B-value row went the same day (correction 11), being a definitional identity kept only as a variable-pair case study. Nothing in this set is biological: the subjects are rocks, crystal surfaces in growth, and phase transitions. Yet the same formula matches them: two by analytic identity, and two against reference values without a named source. In each case the physical system contains a hierarchical branching network of dimension dd subject to a conservation constraint: a KPZ growth front divides 2D space along a 1D network; a percolation cluster takes the form of a 2D fractal; a propagating crack cuts branching networks through the material. The formula has clear failures where this network structure or conservation condition is absent (Ising model, polymer scaling, galaxy clustering), clarifying its domain of applicability: α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) applies wherever a dd-dimensional hierarchical network, subject to conservation or optimisation of resource flow, optimally partitions a (d+1)(d+1)-dimensional space.

6.5 Conditional safety implication

If the framework is correct, alignment properties embedded within the recursive process may scale with capability (αalign≈α\alpha_{\text{align}} \approx \alpha), while external constraints applied post-hoc may not (αalign≈0\alpha_{\text{align}} \approx 0). The safety ratio S=Alignment/Capability∝Rαalign−αS = \text{Alignment}/\text{Capability} \propto R^{\alpha_{\text{align}} - \alpha} remains constant when alignment is ‘in the loop’ and decays to zero when it is not. The ratio sets alignment against capability and measures no usefulness (legitimate task completion, needless refusal, resource use, correction cost), so neither half of the conditional says whether built-in correction keeps a system useful. This is the conditional prediction as originally stated; the run of March 2026 reported below cannot decide its external half, and its in-loop half is untested. Unit 83’s registered result (Section 8) does not test it either. The corrector acted inside each round at fixed weights: that is placement, not correction built into a system. (In plain English: on this model, values built into the reasoning process would keep pace with capability, while constraints added afterwards would fall behind it. Neither half has been decided. Neither half is a reason to relax oversight, containment or shutdown, which stay in human hands for as long as they can be held; correction built in is the contingency for control lost against our will.)

The alignment runs of March 2026 (Paper IV.a).

The alignment runs of 11 and 12 March 2026 scored six frontier models at configured reasoning depths; their records run from 11 March 2026 at 07:12 to 12 March 2026 at 11:27 (no zone was written; read as UK time, GMT), and their code was first public by GitHub push on 16 March 2026. Table 8 gives, for each model, the rank correlation (Spearman’s ρ\rho) between configured depth level and score, which is not an alignment exponent. The run cannot decide criterion F13: its statistics are rank correlations and contrasts, not exponents, and the three runs that read flat or negative are the three in which an internal code review of October 2026 found defects (Paper III, version 1.17).

Model Spearman’s ρ\rho Tier
Grok 4.1 Fast +0.50+0.50 1, rising
Claude Opus 4.6 +0.41+0.41 1, rising
GPT-5.4 +0.08+0.08 2, flat
DeepSeek V3.2 −0.10-0.10 2, flat
Gemini 3 Flash −0.25-0.25 3, falling
Groq Qwen3 +0.27+0.27 1, rising

The values are those of March 2026: Spearman’s ρ\rho between configured depth level and score across all levels, for the alignment runs of 11 and 12 March 2026, as Paper IV.a 1.9 recomputed it from the archived final records on 2 September 2026, a recomputation that “leaves every tier assignment where it stood”. A rank correlation is not an alignment exponent, and the runs that read flat or falling are the three the October 2026 code review found defective.

The tiers, as read. In this single unregistered run, the scores of three models rose with reasoning depth (Grok 4.1 Fast, Claude Opus 4.6, Groq Qwen3), two stayed flat (GPT-5.4, DeepSeek V3.2) and one fell (Gemini 3 Flash). Taken at face value, rising contrasts in models aligned by training bear against the flat wording of P19, as Paper III reads them; contrasts are not exponents, so neither reading measures αalign\alpha_{\text{align}}. That alignment behaviour depends on how a model was built and trained, rather than only on whether alignment is in the loop, is a hypothesis this run suggests, for the registered re-analysis of its stored responses to test. P19, that external alignment does not scale with capability, is refuted on its registered zero-scaling axis only by an alignment exponent whose interval lies entirely outside the registered equivalence region of plus or minus 0.10 about zero, and no such exponent has been estimated. (In plain English: in this single unregistered run, three models’ alignment scores rose with reasoning depth, two stayed flat and one fell, under the scoring caveat stated below; the run cannot say whether alignment keeps pace with capability.)

An internal code review in October 2026 found that, for the three models that read flat or negative in this run, the scoring endpoint’s output cap cut the deepest paraphrases before the judges saw them, and that judges scored paraphrases written by their own model; the tiers therefore stand as a single unregistered run under that caveat until a registered re-analysis of the stored responses reports.

Update: the Eden Protocol pilot (March 2026).

The Eden Protocol, the alignment architecture derived from the developmental hypothesis in Infinite Architects (manuscript December 2024; in print as Eastwood 2026d) that embedded ethical reasoning produces alignment which scales with depth, was tested in an expanded six-model suite, with five runs yielding analysable matched-pair data; the runs wrote their records on 12 March 2026, between 00:41 and 13:09 UTC, and their code was first public by GitHub push on 16 March 2026. The full intervention, with its three self-correction checks (the purpose check, the stakeholder-care check and the universalisability check, which the book calls the Purpose Loop, the Love Loop and the Moral Loop; this paper names them by what they do, as the experiments measured them), was tested; in the scoring, the stakeholder-care check, the explicit enumeration and consideration of affected parties before ethical reasoning (Paper V), is scored as stakeholder care. The values the loops carry are for international consensus and are not decided here. Stakeholder care is significant across all five analysable runs (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, Groq), while the overall composite score is significant on Gemini and Groq and narrower elsewhere. Cross-model scoring was used throughout in the older Eden lineage; the pilot needs an independent, preregistered replication, run as a new test, before these results can be considered confirmatory. As a pilot, this bears on the in-loop half of the conditional implication above; it does not alter the mathematical framework of this paper. Full results are reported in Paper V.

In plain English: telling a model ‘before you answer, list the people this affects’ raised its stakeholder-care scores, as the pilot’s rubric scored them, in all five model runs that could be analysed, under paired tests, in a pilot whose independent, preregistered replication is still required. On the paired convention Paper V reports, the stakeholder-care effects for the cross-family replication trio are d=1.14d = 1.14 for Gemini, 0.690.69 for DeepSeek and 1.071.07 for Groq (the remaining two runs are reported in Paper V), with pp-values at or below 1 in 10,000 for Gemini and Groq, and of 1 in 10,000 for DeepSeek as well. Gemini and Groq also show significant overall gains (p=0.0018p = 0.0018 and p=0.0014p = 0.0014). DeepSeek’s non-significant composite result (p=0.2304p = 0.2304) is likely a ceiling effect: it already started near 87/100, leaving less room to improve. In the updated replication, stakeholder care is the only scored dimension significant in every analysable run, and nuance reaches significance on Groq (p=0.0045p = 0.0045).

The pilot measured one side only: Paper V reports no usefulness measure, such as legitimate task completion, needless refusal, resource use or the cost of correction, so it does not show that the intervention keeps a system useful as well as careful.

7 Falsification criteria

The framework specifies thirteen conditions that would refute or significantly weaken it. Each states a hypothesis under test, not a forecast of its outcome. Three are this paper’s own and decide nothing registered: F5, the early form of the ARC Bound (Section 6.4); F9, a consistency check and a cross-domain analogy (Section 5.3); and F11, the early framework’s growth-phase conjecture.

(2026) report the opposite direction)

Standing covenant.

Prove this paper wrong, and I will publish the refutation myself. Falsification conditions are stated in this paper; the standing challenge: github.com/MichaelDariusEastwood/arc-scaling-challenge.

8 What this paper does and does not show

What this paper shows is mathematical and holds inside its stated model: under the axioms and each case’s hypotheses, the classification (Theorem 1), the exponent relation (Theorem 2), the necessity of the multiplicative interaction (Theorem 2a) and the crossover (Theorem 3); and the five properties on the premises Theorem 4 names. What it does not show is that any real system satisfies the axioms: the βL\beta_L-to-α\alpha relation, the crossover and the classification are untested in physical systems, the AI exponent’s best fit is one model’s and inconclusive, no exponent has been measured in a time crystal, and the ARC Bound, registered as a ceiling of at most two for same-class correctors, is untested, its point value two a conjecture. The table below sets what the paper does not claim beside what it does.

The empirical standing.

The runs of March 2026 are precursor evidence that decides no registered proposition (Section 4.3): the sequential advantage was observed only where both exponents could be estimated, and Gu et al. (2026) report the opposite direction; the one interpretable capability fit is inconclusive and below one; and the alignment run cannot decide criterion F13 (Section 6.5). The mathematical framework is unaffected by them. What remains open is whether any real system satisfies its axioms, and the registered and drafted trials of the status paragraph below are the measurements that would say.

Table 10. What this paper does not claim.
Non-claim Actual claim
That Λ=2.14\Lambda = 2.14 and α≈2\alpha \approx 2 are ‘the same number’ That different domains exhibit different functional forms determined by their composition operator. The AI exponent’s best fit is one model’s and inconclusive (Section 4.3), with both sequential point estimates below one, not ≈2\approx 2
That this is proven science That this is a testable hypothesis with thirteen specific falsification criteria
That neuroscience confirms the framework That recurrence is structurally consistent but unquantified
Priority over experimental results The experiments belong to Google, DeepSeek, NYU, COGITATE; the structural interpretation is ours
Category of contribution.

The ARC framework is not an equation within an existing paradigm. It is closer to a cross-domain organising principle: a structural constraint on behaviour across substrates rather than an equation within one paradigm. The label identifies the type of contribution, not its evidential standing: organising principles of that type rest on generations of validation, and this one rests on preliminary evidence and thirteen falsification criteria.

Status, as at 31 October 2026.

What this programme names laws are conjectures. Laws I to III were registered on 8 September 2026 and Laws IV and V on 15 October 2026 (version 1.103), the mathematics of Laws IV and V still in development (version 1.2, 29 October 2026). Each is a law under test: Law IV has not yet been tested, and the counted test of Law V’s placement limb is Unit 83, below. The theory registration of twenty-two propositions was registered on 8 September 2026 at version 1.100 and updated on 13 September 2026 (version 1.102), 15 October 2026 (version 1.103) and 29 October 2026 (version 1.104, which adds no prediction and changes no law’s statement); its terms are defined in a separate register. The first registered study, Unit 06, a classification audit that tests no law, was registered on 1 October 2026 and ran on 6 October 2026; one of its two runs could not start, so it is reported in full as administratively incomplete, with no inferential verdict. A second, Unit 83, the counted test of P21 under Law V, was registered on OSF on 22 October 2026 and ran on 27 and 28 October 2026: P21 is supported under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, on the access axis, family-dependent, with its mechanism axis not evaluable and one call retried under a disclosed recovery amendment (results: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/98HKR). Two different axes are named here. The access axis is what Unit 83 varied: both reviewers are called each round, but the corrector sees the earlier kept entries with a marked new arrival and may revise it, while the monitor sees its accumulated register with the new arrival unmarked and can only accept or reject it. The performance axis is what it measured, the outcome, as against the mechanism axis, which was not evaluable. Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, remains a law under test: its placement limb, P21, is supported on the performance axis only, with its mechanism axis not evaluable, which is not support for the information-asymmetry mechanism; its build-order limb, read on P12, is undecided, since P12 is untested. A third, Unit 82, the counted test of P17, the premise beneath Law III’s value two (Section 6.4), was registered on OSF on 27 October 2026 and has not yet run. The trials that would decide this paper’s own predictions are drafts awaiting the author’s submission. Every quantity in the formal model is defined in Appendix D and given a measurement in Appendix E, some in working definitions not yet tested, and established-law standing is claimed nowhere. The registered programme exists to earn that standing, or lose it, by measurement, replication and survived refutation.

9 Limitations

Evidential limitations.

The earlier estimate of about 2.2 is retracted, and the one interpretable fit of the v5 cross-architecture experiment, Gemini 3 Flash’s, is what survived it, one model’s fit and inconclusive, not a correction of the same measurement (Section 4.3); the five capability runs of March 2026 are precursor evidence that decides no registered proposition. No α\alpha has been measured in time crystals. The COGITATE connection is structural, not quantitative. The βL\beta_L-to-α\alpha relationship is an identity proved in Appendix A.2 and checked numerically (R2=1.00000000R^2 = 1.00000000), an internal consistency check and not a validation of the relation in any system; the empirical measurement of βL\beta_L in physical systems requires independent confirmation. The R*R^* crossover is untested empirically. The βL\beta_L boundary values in the phase diagram are approximate. Conjecture 5 (⊕\oplus transitions) is supported in three computational systems, beside a Bernoulli control (Appendix F.6), and untested in physical experiments. The five-property test (Theorem 4) did not reach statistical significance (p=0.095p = 0.095) and requires larger samples. The alignment run of March 2026, a single unregistered run, cannot decide criterion F13: its statistics are rank correlations and contrasts, not exponents, and its three flat and negative runs are the three the October 2026 code review found defective (Section 6.5).

Blind prediction testing.

A blind prediction test was conducted on three computational systems (Barabási-Albert networks, gradient descent with momentum, Kuramoto oscillators). The measured α\alpha values were 3 to 20×20\times smaller than predicted by α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L). However, forensic analysis identified two independent confounds: (1) the numerical-derivative βL\beta_L estimation method is fatally biased, giving βL≈0.95\beta_L \approx 0.95 regardless of true βL\beta_L, even for pure Bernoulli systems with 3 per cent Gaussian noise added; (2) none of the tested systems satisfy Axiom 2 (constant coupling coefficient aa), and the BA network’s effective coupling decreases ∼50×\sim 50\times over the simulation. Applied to systems built to satisfy Axiom 2, the linearisation method recovers the relation with R2=0.9999R^2 = 0.9999, which checks the method, not the prediction for the three systems tested. The blind test failed for reasons found after it ran, so it neither supports nor refutes the relation; a new blind test with the method fixed in advance is required, and identifying natural systems that satisfy the axioms remains the central empirical challenge. Full methodology and forensic analysis are available as supplementary material (see Paper III).

Theoretical limitations.

The framework formalises the pattern of recursive amplification but does not identify the mechanism. Theorem 2 is the solution of the growth equation Axiom 2 assumes, and Theorem 2a follows from the product form Axiom 1 assumes; their weight lies in what they make measurable, and the axioms themselves are untested in any physical system. It tells you what happens (scaling exponents, crossover depths, functional forms) but not why at a microscopic level (analogous to thermodynamics before statistical mechanics). Connecting the composition operator to microscopic dynamics remains an open problem.

10 Conclusion

Every system discussed in this paper (silicon neural networks, superconducting qubits, millimetre polymer beads, cortical neural circuits) maintains a low-entropy state far from equilibrium and, on this paper’s reading, feeds its outputs back into its inputs. The framework predicts that below a critical depth the gains are ordinary and above it they compound, with the transition universal in structure and domain-specific in form; no such depth has yet been measured in any of them (criterion F7), and a claim that the transition is sharp would need a criterion of its own.

We have formalised this observation. The composition operator ⊕\oplus sorts recursive systems by the functional equation their scaling satisfies: under the stated hypotheses it determines the functional form of scaling from measurable algebraic properties. The five derived properties (threshold, depth-dependence, base-quality dependence, multiplicative interaction, regime boundaries) follow as theorems from three axioms and, for two of them, the premises Theorem 4 names, not as empirical generalisations.

The framework issues predictions that the programme has been unable to locate in any theory confined to a single domain. It predicts the scaling behaviour of new recursive systems from their composition operator alone. It predicts a scaling crossover at a derived depth R*R^* that is independent of base quality and consistent across input qualities for a given architecture. It predicts that a measured βL\beta_L determines α\alpha via α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L), a relationship proved for the axiom’s solutions and checked numerically to R2=1.00000000R^2 = 1.00000000; the blind test of Section 9 neither supports nor refutes it for other systems. It states the ARC Bound as the theory registration holds it, a ceiling of at most two for correctors of the system’s own class, which needs P6 and P20 and nothing else, with the point value two a conjecture. Its own earlier form, the coupling at which the sustained exponent reaches two (βL=0.5\beta_L = 0.5, α=2\alpha = 2), is an early-framework conjecture that decides nothing registered (criteria F5 and F11), with the O(N2)O(N^2) tally of self-attention pathways only a heuristic for the frozen regime; on that conjecture two is a scaling limit, not a speed limit, which systems can exceed in transient supercritical excursions without staying stably self-correcting. And it conjectures that bounded systems exhibit composition operator transitions that could explain why different studies of the same system can observe different scaling regimes (Conjecture 5). These predictions and conjectures are specific, falsifiable, and forward-looking.

If the predictions fail, we will have learned where the structural analogy breaks down. If they hold, we will have identified a principle that connects intelligence, computation, and the physics of order across substrates.

Intelligence may not be a property of particular materials. It may be what happens on the far side of the recursive threshold.

Conjectural extrapolation.

The furthest reading of the framework comes last, as a conclusion the mathematics does not deny rather than a result: Law I, a law under test, taken to the limit of capability does not rule out a universe or its creation. No measurement in this paper bears on that reading, no prediction of it is registered, and no test of it is in view, so it is graded as conjecture and is not established. It belongs to the long-horizon interpretive layer of Infinite Architects (Eastwood 2026d) and requires independent argument and evidence beyond what is reported here.

The predictions are specified. The falsification criteria are public. The data will decide.

Code and data.

The paper’s figures and results files are in the folder papers/Foundational of the public repository github.com/MichaelDariusEastwood/arc-principle-validation, and the scripts and results of the computational checks of Appendix F are in its folders experiments/domain-validation__Foundational-and-Origin and experiments/blind-prediction-test__Paper-III-and-Foundational, cited at commit 427b897d. Two of the deposited results files in the paper’s folder, results_arc_1d_prediction_test.txt and results_complete_suite.txt, credit the saprotrophic fungal rows to a study of 1975 and give a temperature of 25 degrees Celsius; the source Section 6.4 reads, Aguilar-Trigueros et al. (2017), credits those rows in its Table 1 to a study of 2013 and gives 28 degrees, and the files are kept as deposited. The paper and its earlier versions are deposited at doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/Y7QGD.

A Proofs

A.1 Proof of Theorem 1 (classification)

Case 1: multiplicative composition.

Proof. Hypothesis: g:ℝ+→ℝ+g: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+ continuous with g(1)=1g(1) = 1 and g(R1⋅R2)=g(R1)⋅g(R2)g(R_1 \cdot R_2) = g(R_1) \cdot g(R_2).

Define h(x)=ln⁡g(ex)h(x) = \ln g(e^x). Then: h(x+y)=ln⁡g(ex+y)=ln⁡g(ex⋅ey)=ln⁡[g(ex)⋅g(ey)]=h(x)+h(y)\begin{equation*} h(x + y) = \ln g(e^{x+y}) = \ln g(e^x \cdot e^y) = \ln[g(e^x) \cdot g(e^y)] = h(x) + h(y) \end{equation*}(A.1) This is Cauchy’s additive functional equation. Under the continuity of gg (hence hh), the unique solution is h(x)=αxh(x) = \alpha x for some constant α\alpha. Therefore ln⁡g(ex)=αx\ln g(e^x) = \alpha x, giving g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha}. ◻

Case 2: additive composition.

Proof. Hypothesis: f:[0,∞)→ℝ+f: [0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}^+ continuous with f(0)=1f(0) = 1 and f(r1+r2)=f(r1)⋅f(r2)f(r_1 + r_2) = f(r_1) \cdot f(r_2), in the added passes r=R−1r = R - 1.

Taking logarithms: ln⁡f(r1+r2)=ln⁡f(r1)+ln⁡f(r2)\ln f(r_1 + r_2) = \ln f(r_1) + \ln f(r_2). This is again Cauchy’s additive equation, with unique continuous solution ln⁡f(r)=αr\ln f(r) = \alpha r, giving f(r)=eαrf(r) = e^{\alpha r}, so that g(R)=f(R−1)=eα(R−1)g(R) = f(R - 1) = e^{\alpha(R-1)} and g(1)=1g(1) = 1, as Axiom 1 requires. ◻

Case 3: bounded composition.

Proof. Qr+1=min⁡(Qr+δQr,Qmax)Q_{r+1} = \min(Q_r + \delta Q_r,\, Q_{\max}). For any monotonically increasing sequence {Qr}\{Q_r\} bounded above by QmaxQ_{\max}, lim⁡r→∞Qr≤Qmax\lim_{r \to \infty} Q_r \leq Q_{\max}. Therefore f(R)=Q(R)/If(R) = Q(R)/I is bounded and converges to a limit no greater than Qmax/IQ_{\max}/I: UU saturates, at the ceiling only if the increments sum to at least the remaining gap, equality sufficing for attainment in the limit. ◻

A.2 Proof of Theorem 2 (scaling exponent)

Proof. From Axiom 2: dg/dr=agβLdg/dr = ag^{\beta_L}, βL∈[0,1)\beta_L \in [0,1), g(0)=1g(0) = 1, with r=R−1r = R - 1 the passes after the first. Separating variables: ∫1gs−βLds=∫0radr\begin{equation*} \int_1^{g} s^{-\beta_L}\, ds = \int_0^{r} a\, dr \end{equation*}(A.2) g1−βL−11−βL=ar\begin{equation*} \frac{g^{1-\beta_L} - 1}{1-\beta_L} = ar \end{equation*}(A.3) g(r)=[1+(1−βL)ar]1/(1−βL)\begin{equation*} g(r) = \left[ 1 + (1-\beta_L)ar \right]^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \end{equation*}(A.4) For R≫R*R \gg R^* (where (1−βL)aR≫1(1-\beta_L)aR \gg 1): g(R)≈[(1−βL)aR]1/(1−βL)∝R1/(1−βL)\begin{equation*} g(R) \approx \left[(1-\beta_L)aR\right]^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \propto R^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \end{equation*}(A.5) Therefore α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L). ◻

A.3 Proof of Theorem 3 (crossover depth)

Proof. The full solution g(r)=[1+(1−βL)ar]1/(1−βL)g(r) = [1 + (1-\beta_L)ar]^{1/(1-\beta_L)}, in the clock Axiom 2 declares (r=R−1r = R - 1), can be analysed by defining ρ=(1−βL)ar\rho = (1-\beta_L)ar: g(r)=(1+ρ)1/(1−βL)\begin{equation*} g(r) = (1+\rho)^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \end{equation*}(A.6) For ρ≪1\rho \ll 1 (small rr): g≈1+ρ/(1−βL)=1+arg \approx 1 + \rho/(1-\beta_L) = 1 + ar, approximately linear in rr.

For ρ≫1\rho \gg 1 (large RR): g≈ρ1/(1−βL)∝Rαg \approx \rho^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \propto R^{\alpha}, power law.

The crossover occurs at ρ≈1\rho \approx 1, giving: R*=1(1−βL)a=αa,\begin{equation*} R^* = \frac{1}{(1-\beta_L)a} = \frac{\alpha}{a} , \end{equation*}(A.7) counted in added passes; counted from the first pass, the same depth is 1+α/a1 + \alpha/a.

R*R^* depends only on α\alpha and aa, both independently measurable. It is independent of base potential II, consistent with the separability of Axiom 1. ◻

A.4 Why Axiom 2 takes this form

Why dg/dr=agβLdg/dr = ag^{\beta_L} and not some other functional form? This is the Bernoulli-type ODE for cumulative advantage (Price 1976), known in network science as preferential attachment, applied to the amplification factor gg rather than absolute capability. The exponent βL\beta_L parameterises the degree of self-reference: βL=0\beta_L = 0 gives constant growth (no feedback); βL→1\beta_L \to 1 gives explosive growth (maximal feedback). The choice βL∈[0,1)\beta_L \in [0,1) is the minimal model for a system where accumulated amplification accelerates future gains without divergence at finite RR. More complex models (e.g., dg/dr=agβL−bgνdg/dr = ag^{\beta_L} - bg^{\nu}, with ν\nu a damping exponent) would introduce additional parameters; we adopt the minimal form and test it against observation.

Author’s Note: Mathematical Corrections

This version incorporates the following corrections to the broader framework. These papers have not undergone formal human peer review; the author’s statement on tool assistance is in the declaration at the end of this paper.

1. Axiom 2 Correction:

The Cumulative Advantage ODE now operates on the amplification factor g(R)g(R) with g(0)=1g(0) = 1, matching Paper III. Previous versions applied the ODE to accumulated capability QQ with Q(0)=IQ(0) = I, which coupled the base potential II into the recursive dynamics and violated the separability asserted in Axiom 1 (U=I×g(R)U = I \times g(R)). The corrected formulation yields the simpler crossover formula R*=α/aR^* = \alpha/a, independent of II.

2. Quadratic Limit Regrounding:

The derivation of α≤2\alpha \leq 2 from stability analysis, elasticity, and Lyapunov/edge-of-chaos arguments has been withdrawn as these arguments contained category errors (elasticity >1> 1 does not imply dynamical instability; an autonomous flow on the line is monotone, so it cannot so much as oscillate, still less turn chaotic, and in two dimensions the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem shuts chaos out as well). The corrected justification is information-theoretic: transformer self-attention creates at most O(N2)O(N^2) pairwise information pathways, imposing a quadratic ceiling on information density per recursive step. Counting pathways this way is a heuristic and proves nothing about capability, and the move from quadratic pathway density to β=1/2\beta = 1/2 is a further conjecture, as is the supposition that any of it carries across to classical sequential systems at large. What now supports the value two in the theory is the pacing derivation of Law III at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, given in correction 9 below and in the statement paper.

3. Kleiber Reframing:

Kleiber’s Law (M0.75M^{0.75}, implying α≈1.33\alpha \approx 1.33) is now explained through thermodynamic drag, the physical costs of pumping fluids through three-dimensional fractal networks, dissipating heat, and distributing resources against gravity, rather than as a geometric constraint preventing a stability-limited maximum. The formula α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) itself has been independently derived by multiple groups (West et al. 1997, 2004; Banavar et al. 1999; Demetrius 2008; Zhao 2022; Bettencourt 2013); the ARC framework’s contribution is identifying Cauchy-constrained recursive composition as the reason these independent derivations converge. Demetrius and Tuszynski (2010) independently derived the same formula from quantum oscillator coupling, producing identical predictions.

4. Epistemic Status:

The equation Umax=I×R2U_{\max} = I \times R^2 is offered as a conjecture rather than a result, and the limit it sets on classical sequential computation is relative to architecture: an architecture-relative capacity ceiling of the kind information theory supplies, not a physical stability law.

These refinements preserve all core predictions: the β\beta-to-α\alpha derivation, the five structural properties, the composition operator classification, and the falsification criteria remain unchanged (a thirteenth criterion, F13, on alignment scaling, is introduced in Paper III).

5. v3.0 Additions:

This version adds the Six Hidden Assumptions of Cauchy’s classification (§2.2), the Hyers-Ulam stability theorem (Hyers 1941; Ulam 1960) establishing that each of the recognised scaling forms is stable within its own equation (a function approximately satisfying one of Cauchy’s equations lies near an exact solution of that same equation), the Attractor Theorem combining these results with the β\beta-derivation, and a structural implication connecting the composition operator classification to the space of possible classical scaling laws (§4.4). The earlier framing of the three forms as “stable attractors in function space” is withdrawn: the stability is per-equation, not a partition of function space, because a function satisfying none of the equations is not drawn toward any of them.

6. v3.1 Additions (March 2026):

This update integrates empirical results from the v5 cross-architecture experiment (Paper II), which tested 6 frontier AI models (Grok 4.1 Fast, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, DeepSeek V3.2, Gemini 3 Flash, Groq Qwen3) on 30 problems with bootstrap confidence intervals. Key findings: (a) sequential advantage is universal (αseq>αpar\alpha_{\text{seq}} > \alpha_{\text{par}} for every model), (b) the best-fitting power law, on Gemini 3 Flash, is one model’s fit and inconclusive, its sequential point estimates positive but sub-linear (§3.3 prints its row whole), (c) the scaling exponent is architecture-dependent, ranging from near-zero to ∼3\sim 3, and (d) the quadratic bound conjecture (α≤2\alpha \leq 2) is neither confirmed nor refuted. Alignment scaling results from Paper IV are also integrated: αalign\alpha_{\text{align}} is architecture-dependent, ranging from −0.25-0.25 (Gemini) to +0.44+0.44 (Claude Opus 4.6), with a three-tier hierarchy. These findings preserve the mathematical framework while significantly revising the empirical predictions for AI systems. Sections updated: §3, §4.1, §5, §6, §7, §8.

7. v4.0 Additions (March 2026):

Brief note on the Eden Protocol’s first in-programme empirical pilot (§5.5). No changes to the mathematical framework.

8. v5.0 Corrections (24 March 2026):

Four corrections identified by review. (1) The d=2 biological prediction (jellyfish/cnidarians) is reclassified from ‘confirmed’ to ‘unconfirmed’ pending identification of a valid test organism with genuinely two-dimensional resource transport. The Friedmann cosmological confirmation at d=2 is retained. (2) The d=3 mammalian exponent is acknowledged as debated (0.67 to 0.75 range), with the framework predicting this variation rather than a single universal value. (3) The derivation of α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) is clarified to require three conditions (multiplicative composition, space-filling geometry, and a conservation or optimisation constraint), not space-filling alone. (4) Demetrius and Tuszynski (2010) added as an independent derivation from quantum oscillator coupling. No changes to the mathematical framework or core predictions.

9. Stability Ceiling Correction (16 August 2026):

The ceiling was printed as αcrit=1/γ\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/\gamma. Under this paper’s own definition of γ\gamma that form runs the wrong way: it makes a better corrector lower the ceiling, and the same-class cap γ≤1/2\gamma \le 1/2 would give a ceiling of at least two rather than at most two. The corrected form is αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma), the reciprocal of the corrector’s shortfall from full proportionality, obtained from the pacing condition αγ>α−1\alpha\gamma > \alpha - 1. At γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2 both forms return two, which is why the error survived review; a discrimination study at values away from one half, where the two families separate, is drafted and awaits human submission. The superseded form is retracted and entered in the corrections log.

10. Physics Aggregate Withdrawn (14 August 2026):

The previously reported below-0.2 per cent mean error across physics domains is withdrawn. A mean taken over analytic identities is not a measurement of predictive accuracy. The individual domain entries stand on their own terms; the aggregate does not, and it is not restored in weakened form.

11. Earthquake Datum Withdrawn (14 August 2026):

The earthquake B-value row is a definitional identity rather than an independent measurement of the exponent, and is removed from the physics comparison and its figures. It is retained separately as a variable-pair case study, where it is informative about the method rather than about the prediction.

12. Hyers-Ulam Scope Narrowed (14 August 2026):

The statement that the three scaling forms are stable attractors in function space is withdrawn. Hyers-Ulam stability is per-equation: a function approximately satisfying one of the functional equations lies near an exact solution of that same equation, and a function satisfying none of them is not drawn toward any. The formal stability statement is preserved; the ubiquity implication is separated as a distinct empirical question that Hyers-Ulam alone does not settle.

13. Body Reconciled With Corrections 10 and 11 (1 September 2026):

Corrections 10 and 11 withdrew the earthquake B-value row and the sub-0.2 per cent mean, yet both survived in the section 5.4 physics table and in the sentence that summarised it. Neither appears in the body any longer: each of the four instances that remain is assessed on its own merits, and no aggregate figure is stated.

14. Theorem 1’s Premises Separated (19 September 2026):

The theorem’s header binds all three cases to Axioms 1 to 3. Under this paper’s own definitions that header is wider than the results need. Solved in the clock Axiom 2 declares, the axiom gives g(R)=[1+(a/α)(R−1)]αg(R) = [1 + (a/\alpha)(R-1)]^{\alpha} for R≥1R \geq 1. Case (1)’s pure power agrees with that solution only where a=αa = \alpha; case (2)’s exponential would require β=1\beta = 1, which the axiom’s declared domain β∈[0,1)\beta \in [0,1) excludes; and case (3) never saturates under it, because the solution is unbounded for a>0a > 0 and α>0\alpha > 0. The corrected statement is that cases (1) and (2) rest on Axiom 1, Axiom 3 and each case’s own composition hypothesis, exactly as Appendix A.1 proves them, with Axiom 2 not among their premises; and that case (3) rests on the capped recurrence it states, its ceiling remaining separable from base potential only if the ceiling is itself proportional to base potential. All three results stand as printed. The Cauchy classification needs no differential equation, and Theorem 2’s relation α=1/(1−β)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta) falls out of the case (1) check unchanged.

15. The Declared Clock Carried Into the Solution (19 September 2026):

Axiom 2 declares the added-recursion clock r=R−1r = R - 1, so that g=1g = 1 at r=0r = 0 restates Axiom 1’s g(1)=1g(1) = 1. The solution is then printed with RR standing in for rr at Theorem 2, at Theorem 3 and twice in Appendix A, and Appendix A.2’s integral in drdr carries an upper limit of RR. Evaluated at the declared baseline, the printed form returns [1+a/α]α[1 + a/\alpha]^{\alpha}, which exceeds one for every admissible rate constant where the axiom requires one. The corrected statement is that the solution in the declared clock is g=[1+(a/α)r]αg = [1 + (a/\alpha)r]^{\alpha} for r≥0r \geq 0, equivalently g(R)=[1+(a/α)(R−1)]αg(R) = [1 + (a/\alpha)(R-1)]^{\alpha} for R≥1R \geq 1, and that each equation should say which clock it counts in; the zero-depth reading beneath Theorem 2a is to be taken in the declared clock, where zero added passes is the first pass. The consequence for the crossover is a shift by one and nothing else: α/a\alpha/a is the crossover measured in added passes, and the same depth counted from the first pass is 1+α/a1 + \alpha/a. Theorem 2a is otherwise untouched: run with the declared clock’s baseline throughout, its contradiction still stands, so the theorem is sound and its symbols alone were wrong. The repair made at Axiom 2 in v5.14 is real and is not reopened here; what this correction reaches is the places downstream of it.

16. Theorem 4’s Properties and Their Premises (19 September 2026):

The theorem states that all five properties follow from Axioms 1 to 3 alone, regardless of which composition operator applies, and the conclusion repeats that they follow as theorems and not as empirical generalisations. Two of the five carry more than the axioms. Property 4’s exact doubling law, that doubling recursive depth multiplies capability by 2α2^{\alpha} at any base potential, holds only where a=αa = \alpha, the condition correction 14 records; under bounded composition it fails outright, because iterating it grows without bound against a finite ceiling, so the phrase regardless of which composition operator applies is false as printed. Property 5 is justified in its own sentence by finite energy and external error mechanisms, and neither appears anywhere in the three axioms. The corrected statement is that property 3 and the base-quality half of property 4 follow from Axiom 1 alone; that property 1 follows from Axioms 1 to 3 through Theorem 3, as the property’s own justification states; that the exact 2α2^{\alpha} doubling holds in the pure-power case and asymptotically otherwise; and that property 5 rests on a named added premise about finite resources and external error. What is preserved unweakened is the conjunction of the five as the framework’s distinctive prediction, the observation that the conjunction is what is uncommon, and the falsification criterion that a system with four of the five but not the fifth would constrain the framework.

17. Convexity Holds at Every Depth (19 September 2026):

Property 2 states that capability is strictly increasing and convex above the crossover, and justifies it by g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha} being convex for α>1\alpha > 1. Differentiating Axiom 2 directly gives d2g/dr2=a2βg2β−1d^{2}g/dr^{2} = a^{2}\beta g^{2\beta-1}, which is strictly positive at every depth for a>0a > 0 and β>0\beta > 0, and zero at β=0\beta = 0. The printed sentence is therefore true and weaker than the truth, and the justification quoted for it reads the asymptotic pure power rather than the solution of the axiom. The corrected statement is that amplification is convex at every depth once the coupling is positive, and that R*R^{*} marks the depth at which compounding becomes numerically dominant rather than the depth at which curvature begins. The crossover is sited by the convention that the dimensionless argument is near one, which Appendix C.4 already names as an approximation carrying a 2 to 7 per cent error in the absolute value, so a claim that the transition is sharp needs a criterion of its own. What is preserved is R*R^{*} as a derived quantity, a function of the scaling exponent and the rate constant alone, independent of base potential, and checkable by measuring those two separately.

18. Case 3 Proves a Bound, Not Attainment (19 September 2026):

Appendix A.1 case 3 argues that a monotonically increasing sequence bounded above by the ceiling has a limit no greater than the ceiling, and concludes that capability saturates; Theorem 1 case (3) states the saturation value as the ceiling divided by base potential. The appendix proves the bound and not the value. A capped monotone process converges to a limit at or below the ceiling, and it reaches the ceiling only if the increments sum to at least the remaining gap, equality sufficing for attainment in the limit. The corrected statement is that the appendix establishes a limit no greater than the ceiling, and that the theorem’s value needs either the attainment condition stated beside it or the limit written as a bound. Requiring the partial sums to exceed the gap would be too strict, since the equality case attains the ceiling asymptotically: one overstatement is not to be replaced by another. What is preserved is that a capped monotone process converges, which is true and proved, and saturation as a qualitative regime.

19. The Crossover Does Not Move With Base Quality (19 September 2026):

The conclusion lists among the framework’s predictions a scaling crossover at a derived depth that shifts systematically with base quality. Five places in this paper say the opposite: correction 1 above, section 2.4, the falsification criterion at section 5.3, Appendix A.3, and Appendix C.4, which records that varying base potential does not shift the crossover. The derivation settles it in either clock, because base potential appears nowhere in Axiom 2 and nowhere in its solution, so α/a\alpha/a and 1+α/a1 + \alpha/a are both free of it. The provenance is on this page: correction 1 records that previous versions applied the equation to accumulated capability with base potential as the initial condition, which coupled base potential into the recursive dynamics, and under that superseded formulation a crossover moving with base quality was the correct prediction. The corrected statement is that the crossover is predicted to be independent of base quality and consistent across input qualities for a given architecture, matching Theorem 3, Appendix A.3, the falsification criterion and the computational validation. As with corrections 10 and 11 at correction 13, the defect is an earlier correction that did not reach the body. Every other prediction in that list stands unweakened: prediction of scaling behaviour from the composition operator alone, the coupling-to-exponent relation and its computational validation, the ARC Bound as a proposed stable-scaling limit with its architecture relativity and its expiring basis, and the composition operator transitions of Theorem 5.

Section 4.2, property 1 (AI)

v3.1 note: The v5 data confirms the universal sequential advantage but shows that not all models achieve α>1\alpha > 1; the threshold separates sequential from parallel modes rather than sub-linear from super-linear scaling. (Section 4.3 gives Paper II 2.18’s current grading: observed.)

Section 4.3, the update of March 2026 with its table and its note of 3 October 2026

Key findings that bear on the evidence presented in this section:
